_marker: RECIPE FIDELITY MANIFEST — every subject scored by npm run recipe:fidelity:check
_note: The check is OFFLINE: it scores committed canvas shots against committed real-package references, so it runs in CI with no Figma access. `npm run recipe:fidelity:capture` re-exports the shots from the live canvas (read-only exportAsync) and is the only step that needs the plugin. A shot and its reference are both committed bytes, so a score is reproducible from the repo alone.
_referenceRule: The reference MUST be orig-shots/ — the real package rendered in Chromium by extract/computed. Never a gate-shot (the pipeline's own re-render) and never another mint. Comparing a mint to a mint measures nothing, and the scorer refuses a gate-shot path outright.
_astryxMountNote: Astryx subjects reference extract/computed/out/astryx-core/, the un-themed @astryxdesign/core mount, because that is the surface recipe/fixtures/library-*.ts transcribes. The themed astryx/ capture mounts <Theme theme={neutralTheme}>, which is a different real surface — scoring against it would fail on the theme rather than on the mint.

subjects.label: checkbox/chakra
subjects._proposedWhy: the Chakra fixture was PROPOSED by recipe/fixture-reader/propose-fixture.ts from the capture ledger (42 leaves read, 3 reviewed, 10 archetype spellings, 0 invented) — the first library the recipe path was pointed at rather than taught

subjects.label: checkbox/shadcn
subjects._proposedWhy: the shadcn fixture was PROPOSED from the capture ledger (28 leaves read, 6 reviewed, 21 archetype spellings, 0 invented) — the first BARE control: no label part, so the recipe's label-less cell; colours declared in oklch and read through the ledger's CSS Color 4 conversion (pinned to the render's own pixels); the indeterminate state draws the check glyph, which checkbox@1 cannot express — a named gap, not scored as a pass

subjects.label: switch/mui
subjects._canvasBoxWhy: MUI's unchecked switch is a thumb at the left of a wider track, with whitespace between them. The leading-control crop rule splits that and measures the thumb alone, so the control's bounds are taken from the scene instead.

subjects.label: switch/antd
subjects._fringeRetired: 2026-09-01: the 44x24-vs-44x22 band was NOT anti-aliasing — it was the handle's real drop shadow (handleShadow 0 2px 4px rgba(0,35,11,.2)) that the hand fixture recorded as none; found by the role schema re-derivation. The row must pass on its own now.

subjects.label: radio/mui
subjects._variantPairing: MUI's radio has a COLOUR axis and the capture's leading segment is that colour, not a default-ness. The fixture carries #1976d2 (primary), so the reference must be primary.*. Pairing it with default.* compared our blue radio to MUI's grey one and read 36% as a mint defect. The Figma variant is Selected=a, so the control is the CHECKED state.

subjects.label: radio/antd
subjects._variantPairing: The Figma variant is Selected=a, so radio/item/a's control is the SELECTED state. It must be scored against the library's CHECKED render; pairing it with unchecked.enabled__default compared our filled radio to their empty one and read 55% as a mint defect.

_excluded.radio/astryx: Astryx ships RadioList, and extract/computed/configs/astryx.json declares no Radio component — there is no real-package render to score against. Not a defect in the mint; a gap in the capture corpus. EYEBALL NOTE, unverified: on the v3 page the Astryx UNSELECTED radio reads as a solid white circle with no visible border, where a radio normally carries one. That may be correct for Astryx or may be a missing stroke — it cannot be decided here, which is the whole point of the exclusion. Capturing Astryx Radio would settle it.
_excluded.dialog/*, menu/*: the only references (mui/dialog, mui/menu) are 900x1000 full-viewport overlay captures with a backdrop, so an ink trim cannot isolate the surface; a surface-only reference capture is needed before these can be scored.
_excluded.button/altitude, input/mui, combobox/mui: the signed pages carry two component sets with IDENTICAL names (one per library leg); the name resolver cannot pick a leg deterministically. Needs a per-leg set rename or a section-scoped resolver. References exist (altitude/button, mui/textfield, mui/autocomplete, mui/table).

_widthNormalisedNote: widthNormalised subjects (fill-width controls) are scored as two equal edge windows after an ink trim: corners, border, radius, label offset and every vertical metric are compared; the interior run of the wider side is not. See recipe/fidelity-score.ts scoreEdgeWindows.
